analysis: Changes are limited to CI path-filter additions and documentation. provider-release-cache.yml (head line 25) adds scripts/check-provider-weak-imports.py to the pull_request paths filter. release-dev-branch.yml (head line 77) and release-swift.yml (head line 72) add the same script to their push path filters. The PR trigger in provider-release-cache.yml has no new permissions, secrets or trust changes. The workflow still runs with contents: read and persist-credentials: false, and the pinned actions are unchanged. The release-dev-branch.yml and release-swift.yml changes only make a change to that script trigger the existing dev or staging lanes. Both lanes are already gated by branch and ref checks, and the prod lane remains tag-gated. Neither file's secrets handling or signing flow changed. The changelog and docs/architecture/inference.md edits are documentation. They describe a Date >=/<= back-deploy crash on pre-release macOS 27.2 and a new release-lane check that refuses binaries importing those symbols; the check is a build-integrity and availability hardening. The script itself (check-provider-weak-imports.py) and its wiring into the build action are not in the supplied evidence, so I could not verify its logic or that it actually gates signing. That is an unverified contract rather than a finding. No impact on the attestation, encryption or coordinator-provider boundary (TB-002, TB-009, TB-011) or on the prefix-cache threat T-041 was identified. The inference.md patch excerpt is truncated but the visible content is a troubleshooting table row.
